title: Refactoring Without Changing Behaviour
learningObjectives: Define refactoring as restructuring while preserving observable behavior.
Distinguish refactoring from feature changes and bug fixes.
Plan small refactoring steps with safety checks.
Use tests or traces to compare behavior before and after.
Recognize risky refactoring changes that alter the contract.

understand.concept: Refactoring improves internal structure without intentionally changing observable behavior. It may rename variables, extract functions, simplify branches, or reduce duplication. Refactoring differs from adding features or fixing behavior: the goal is to make the existing behavior easier to understand or change. Use small steps, keep tests or comparison checks available, and avoid combining unrelated changes. If behavior changes, document and treat it as a separate change rather than claiming a pure refactor.
understand.whyItMatters: Design habits that support clarity, safe changes, and sustainable learning help programs remain understandable as requirements evolve.
understand.analogy: Think of maintaining a shared workspace: clear organization makes it easier to improve without disrupting others.
understand.analogyLimit: Software behavior is governed by language rules and dependencies, so the workspace analogy is only a way to reason about organization.

explain.narrative: Before restructuring, understand the current behavior and capture it with tests, examples, or a trace. Make one structural change at a time and rerun checks. A refactor can accidentally change edge cases, order, timing, or side effects. Preserve the interface unless an intentional interface change is separately planned. A readable diff helps reviewers confirm that only structure changed.

commonMistakes: Confusing a design improvement with a behavior change.
Making abstractions too broad or too narrow.
Ignoring tests and boundary behavior during changes.
Applying a guideline mechanically without considering the project's scale.

guidedTask.title: Guided Practice
guidedTask.instructions: Select a function with duplicated or confusing code. Record outputs for normal and boundary inputs. Make one refactoring change such as extracting a helper or renaming. Rerun the same checks and compare outputs. Review the diff to confirm no intended behavior was added or removed.
steps: Select a function with duplicated or confusing code.
Record outputs for normal and boundary inputs.
Make one refactoring change such as extracting a helper or renaming.
Rerun the same checks and compare outputs.
Review the diff to confirm no intended behavior was added or removed.

independentTask.title: Independent Practice
independentTask.instructions: Choose a small program with at least one maintainability issue. Capture three inputs and their outputs before changes. Refactor in multiple small steps, recording each change. Run the same checks after each step. Submit before/after code and explain how behavior was preserved.

Run the same checks after each step.

hints: Refactoring changes structure, not the intended result.
Run tests or traces after each step.
Separate feature changes and bug fixes from refactoring.
